Explain what vision-based tracking is and list its optical sensor categories.
Describe infrared tracking and its outside-in and inside-out configurations.
Classify visible light tracking into fiducial, natural feature, and model-based methods.
Explain fiducial tracking using artificial landmarks and fiducial designs.
Explain natural feature tracking using feature descriptors and pose matching.
Explain model-based tracking using SLAM and its PTAM variant.
Describe 3D structure tracking using depth sensors and models for pose estimation and augmentation.
Explain inertial tracking sensors, what they measure, and their limitations.
Introduce additional tracking methods and explain GPS-based location tracking, including RTK and limitations.
Explain motion capture as a wearable tracking approach for recording human movement.
Describe eye-tracking systems and techniques for measuring user gaze.
Explain hybrid trackers that combine multiple basic tracking methods.
Summarize the tracking technologies covered and preview the next lecture on VR software.
